title: Triangulatedness for a chosen finite-extension shift
statement: For l, E, L, ι, X as in [def-sf-integral-finite-extension-core], let T be the chosen scalar functor of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For a coherent shift c on T, if Qh ⋙ T is triangulated using c, then T is triangulated using that same c.

statement_change.old_statement: For l, E, L, ι and X satisfying the hypotheses of [def-sf-integral-finite-extension-core], and for any CommShift c on integralScalarExtensionOfUniverses l E L ι X, that functor is IsTriangulated.
statement_change.what: Coherence of a shift comparison does not imply exactness. Twist an exact comparison by (-1)^n. For identity coefficient extension at l=3 on complete coefficient modules, the triangle of the nonsplit sequence Z_3 --3--> Z_3 --> F_3 has nonzero connecting class delta. The twisted comparison sends its last arrow to -delta with the first two arrows fixed; since 2 delta is nonzero this is not distinguished. The blueprint requires existence of an exact shift, not exactness for every coherent shift.
